simple.meaning: רְחַץ (rᵉchats) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to attend upon.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 3:28. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רְחַץ (H7365) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: רְחַץ (rᵉchats) / H7365 is traced through Daniel 3:28 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Nebuchadnezzar spoke and said, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent his angel, and delivered his servants who trusted in him, and have changed the king’s word, and have yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own God.
